audit.whatIsWrong: Every early-lane line credits Talon's W with the terrain jump, and phases[3].side disagreed with win[3].
audit.why: Rake is W (9s at rank 1, 650, daggers out and back). The vault is Assassin's Path (E, 725, effectively no cooldown but the used terrain goes on a long one). Naming the wrong slot means the reader watches the wrong cooldown.
audit.corrected: Vault attributed to Assassin's Path throughout; Rake described as the poke and its 9s cooldown given as the step-up clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes never mention Blade's End, which is what actually kills Anivia.
audit.why: Talon's spells stack Wound up to 3; the auto that lands on the third stack applies heavy damage over time. Against an egg that is the difference between surviving the burst and bleeding out after it.
audit.corrected: Three-stack bleed written into the spike, the bad trade and the from-behind line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states that Crystallize is terrain Assassin's Path can vault.
audit.why: Anivia's W creates terrain and Talon's E vaults over any terrain. A wall dropped behind Talon is an exit he did not previously have; a wall dropped on his approach still costs him the terrain's long cooldown.
audit.corrected: Wall usage now specifies walling his entry rather than his retreat.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit file flags Rake as a knockup.
audit.why: Riot's own description of Rake says the returning blades deal bonus damage and SLOW — no displacement. Per the brief's own rule, the description wins over a derived flag.
audit.corrected: No knockup claimed anywhere; Rake treated as poke plus slow.

edits.before: Talon's W lets him leap from any nearby brush or wall into an instant burst combo, and since your kit has no hard escape before level 6, this is one of the scariest early windows against you. He wants to poke with Rake, wait for a mistake, then all-in from stealth-adjacent positioning, so ward every brush near mid and never stand still without vision. Play for safe CS and avoid extending past minions where his jump range threatens a full trade.
edits.after: Talon's Assassin's Path lets him vault any nearby wall into an instant burst combo, and since your kit has no hard escape before level 6, this is one of the scariest early windows against you. He wants to poke with Rake, stack Blade's End, then all-in and let the bleed finish it, so watch the side walls and never stand still without vision. Play for safe CS and avoid extending past minions, where his 575-range Q leap turns one step into a full trade.

edits.before: Level 6 helps you answer his dive: Glacial Storm's zone and slow let you punish him the instant he commits to W, since he loses his follow-up mobility after the jump. Use Storm reactively rather than proactively, waiting for his engage before dropping it, and hold Wall to block his approach lane entirely when you can predict it. He remains a roam threat with Rake's range, so ping when he leaves lane.
edits.after: Level 6 helps you answer his dive: Glacial Storm's zone and slow let you punish him the instant he vaults in, since Assassin's Path puts that piece of terrain on a long cooldown and he cannot leave the way he arrived. Use Storm reactively rather than proactively, waiting for his engage before dropping it, and hold Wall to block his approach lane entirely when you can predict it. He roams through the jungle walls, so ping when he leaves.

notes: The vault was attributed to W (Rake) in six places; it is E, Assassin's Path. Rake is W and is poke plus a slow — the kit file's 'knockup' flag on Rake contradicts Riot's own description of the ability and was not used. The Crystallize/Assassin's Path terrain interaction (your wall is something he can vault) is stated as Medium confidence: it follows directly from Riot's 'vaults over any terrain' wording, but the kits do not confirm player-created terrain specifically. phases[3].side 'Skill' disagreed with win[3] 'Talon' and the packet chart; fixed full-layer only since content already matched.
